column1: # data-tu-order baseline: ordinary-data defs that land inside another
# TU's same-storage band (known scattered singletons / accepted homes).
# 0x0020d2e8 was NOT a new interleave - it was UNMASKED on 2026-08-09. This audit
# defaults an unenrolled DATA rva's storage to "data", and Warlord.cpp's
# joined Warlord's `.data` band and stretched it to 0x244610 - swallowing enough
# foreign defs to classify the band a POOL, which EXEMPTS it. Sizing the 51
# template statics moved s_table to the `.bss` band, Warlord's real `.data` band
# [0x20d1bc,0x20d374] reappeared, and the crossing under it became visible.
# The crossing itself is real and pre-existing: 0x20d2e8 holds "F\0" and sits one
# datum below Warlord.cpp's own s_keyE (0x20d2ec), inside Warlord's string run,
# yet our DATA() pin for it is on GruntCombat.cpp's `char s_codeF[] = "F"` while
# Warlord.cpp's `static const char s_keyF[] = "F"` is unpinned. GruntCombat's
# other string static, s_codeH, is at 0x20d7fc - four hundred bytes away - so the
# retail owner of 0x20d2e8 is Warlord.cpp, and the two source spellings are one
# /Gf-pooled retail datum modelled twice. Deciding which spelling keeps the pin is
# a data-attribution call for the pinning lanes, not this audit's.
# The three rows added 2026-08-09 (0x20b8b8, 0x21ab20, 0x21ab24) were unmasked the
# same way, by the same two mechanisms, and NO definition moved to produce them:
#     in the manifest under two owners, which correctly makes it COMDAT - and a
#     COMDAT is linker-pooled, not linearly TU-attributed, so it leaves the band
#     model. WwdObjMgr.cpp's `.data` band shrank from [0x20bdc4,0x21ab30] (a POOL,
#   * the audit now takes an unenrolled rva's storage from the PE instead of
#     defaulting it to "data", which stopped BootyStateActivate.cpp's `.data` band
#     being dragged down over its `.rdata` globals at 0x1e8fe4. (That default was
#     also inventing a crossing: `AttractState.cpp` 0x20b5bc is no longer one.)
# Both remaining crossings are real TU-attribution defects, stated here as the
#     level-message layout data that retail emitted from ONE obj, split across two
#     `?g_fmtPathJoin@@3PBDB`), so at most one of the three owns that run.
# The 28 rows added 2026-08-09 for `Grunt.cpp .data` were UNMASKED, not created:
# every one of them is a `DATA()` pin that predates the change, on a declaration
# the change did not touch. Modelling the strings four TUs share as the /Gf-pooled
# literals they are (`"Grunt"` 0x20a9ec, `"A"` 0x20a454, ...) put those rvas under
# SEVERAL owners, which is what makes this audit treat an rva as COMDAT - and a
# COMDAT leaves the linear band model. Grunt.cpp's `.data` band therefore stopped
# reaching down to 0x20a454, shrank to its real [0x20d414,0x20dfd0], stopped
# swallowing enough foreign defs to be classified a POOL (which EXEMPTS a band),
# and the crossings already inside it became visible.
# They are one family and one defect: a single contiguous retail run of bute keys,
# sound-act names and animation names at [0x20d414,0x20dfd0] that our partition
# pins across FOUR .cpp files - Grunt.cpp owns the band, while GruntCombat.cpp
# (`s_ToyTiles`) claim addresses inside it. Retail emitted that run from ONE obj.
# The likely resolution is the same one this commit applied elsewhere: the shared
# ones are pooled literals with no per-TU array at all, and the rest belong to
# whichever .cpp owns the band. Recorded as the worklist it is.
